If the youth was discharged from care after October 7, 2008: - the letter will be sent to the last known address of the youth. If the case is still open: - Administration and Management will send a copy of the letter to the youth's assigned Administrator for insertion in the youth's case record.

If the case is closed and the record is in the record room: - a copy of the letter will be sent to the record room to be included in the youth's case record.

DHS Worker Responsibilities: For youth aged 16 and older who are still in placement and for whom there is no planned discharge: - The DHS worker will continue referring these youth to the Achieving Independence Center. There is no change in this procedure from the existing practice. Notification of Chafee and ETG benefits will occur through the aforementioned A&M and mailing process. - A copy of the letter notifying the youth/caregiver about the Chafee and ETG benefits will be inserted in the specific child's case record.

For youth aged 16 and older who were discharged from placement to adoption, PLC, or independence as of October 7, 2008 and after and the record has not been sent to the Record Room: - A copy of the letter notifying the youth/caregiver about the Chafee and ETG benefits will be inserted in the specific child's case record.

Note: When the copy of the Chafee benefits letter is received by the DHS worker and it needs to be translated, the worker will submit the letter for document translation services, insert a copy of the original letter and a copy of the translated letter into the child's case record, and mail the translated letter.

Provider worker responsibilities: For youth who are 16 and older and who are scheduled to exit the system to adoption or PLC from the time that this policy and procedural guide is issued and forward: - Prior to finalization of an adoption or a Permanent Legal Custodianship (PLC) for a youth age 16 and

the provider agency must provide written notification to the youth and prospective custodian or adoptive parent. Providers must develop a letter based on the model letter attached to this policy. The letter should be signed by the provider and must accompany all PLC family profiles and adoption home studies in order for these documents to be approved. - Providers will submit a copy of the signed letter to the DHS worker to be inserted in the youth's case

The Education and Training Grant (ETG) Program: The ETG Program generally provides Vouchers of up to five thousand dollars ($5,000) per student annually for post-secondary education or training programs. Interested youth ages 16-20 may apply by completing the Federal Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and the Education and Training Grant (ETG) Program Application. To be eligible for those benefits, the youth must apply no later then age 21. Youth may access these benefits and obtain forms and information by visiting or calling the: Achieving Independence Center (AIC) 1118 Market Street, 2nd floor Philadelphia, PA 19107-3601 215-574-9194 Questions regarding this Guide may be addressed to:

Samuel Harrison III, Policy and Planning Administrator Bari Rose-Epstein, Policy and Planning Supervisor June de Vries, Policy and Planning Program Analyst
